target.name: Parallel Systems
target.founder: Matt Soule, John Howard, Ben Stabler

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $25M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Parallel Systems is a Series B-stage transportation company that has raised $100M to date. The broader transportation sector comp universe includes eight private peers (Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Arc Boats, The ePlane Company, and others) and no public comparables, reflecting the early-stage nature of frontier transportation ventures.

A single valuation method was applicable to this analysis. Stage-progression analysis anchors to the $25M proxy derived from total capital raised and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B-to-next-stage progression, yielding an implied valuation of $48M. Peer-median analysis could not be applied due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow transportation subsector—while three peers exist in Transportation overall, none met the threshold of three or more datapoints within tightly filtered cohorts, rendering a sectoral median unreliable.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $40M to $55M, with a median point of $48M. This range reflects moderate bandwidth around a single applicable method and the absence of secondary validation. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the 1.9x step-up multiplier for frontier transportation specifically, the relevance of the broader peer set given Parallel Systems' particular subsector focus, and the precision of the total-raised proxy as a valuation anchor for a capital-intensive, pre-revenue or early-revenue stage company.
